note: All instructional text and numeric transfer pairs are authored, NOT the printed original Q003. Exact original remains private and SHA-gated by prepare_private.py.
title: One consistent square-offset rule across pairs
inferential_jump: For each ordered pair (x, y), compute the same residual y - x^2. A claimed square-offset rule is coherent only when the residual stays constant; one dissenting pair is the exception.
entry_assumptions: Can square a small positive integer and subtract it from another integer.
Can keep ordered-pair input and output positions fixed.

teaching_path.action: For every ordered pair, keep the first coordinate as input x and the second as output y.
teaching_path.why_valid: Reversing or relabelling an input-output pair changes the relation being tested.
teaching_path.output: A fixed list of (x, y) observations, with source option order unchanged.

teaching_path.action: Compute y - x^2 for each pair without changing the formula between pairs.
teaching_path.why_valid: If one relation is y = x^2 + k, algebraically the same constant k must equal y - x^2 for every member of the matching group.
teaching_path.output: One numerical offset for every pair and a candidate common k.

teaching_path.action: Compare every offset, explain the lone mismatch, then try the same procedure on new authored pairs.
teaching_path.why_valid: A single counterexample falsifies the claim that the same proposed relation fits all displayed pairs; a changed-offset case checks transfer instead of answer memorisation.
teaching_path.output: A justified exception and a repeatable same-rule check on unfamiliar pairs.

teaching_path.action: Run the identical residual procedure on a new, explicitly authored list with a different common offset.
teaching_path.why_valid: A transferable test preserves the subtraction procedure while allowing the new examples to determine their own common constant; reusing a remembered exception would not check understanding.
teaching_path.output: The learner checks the newly authored pairs using one unchanged residual expression, determines the common offset and identifies any exceptional pair independently.

misconceptions.wrong_idea: Choose a different offset or operation for each option until every pair appears to fit.
misconceptions.diagnostic_prompt: Which exact formula, unchanged, did you use for every pair? Write the four residuals.
misconceptions.repair: Choose one candidate form, compute y - x^2 for each input-output pair and reject a single mismatch without altering the form.

misconceptions.wrong_idea: One matching input-output pair proves a universal rule.
misconceptions.diagnostic_prompt: Can the same offset be checked against each other pair before selecting an exception?
misconceptions.repair: One example suggests a candidate; all displayed cases must be tested, and a different list may require a fresh candidate.

construction_units.decision: Compute the same square-offset residual for every pair instead of guessing from one example.

independent_checks.statement: For each ordered pair compute output minus (input squared); state the candidate constant before choosing a mismatch.

construction_units.decision: Reject a single inconsistent pair by testing one unchanged relation, then transfer to different authored numbers.

independent_checks.statement: Re-evaluate all displayed pairs with the same candidate offset; exactly one mismatch must be identified and explained.

authored_transfer.title: Authored changed-offset transfer — not an original IMO question
authored_transfer.stem: AUTHORED TRANSFER (not the original Q003). For the ordered pairs (4, 23), (6, 43), (7, 58), and (9, 88), test whether a single rule y = x^2 + k fits three of the four pairs. Find k, identify the exceptional pair, and show the residual for every pair.
authored_transfer.answer_summary: The common rule is y = x^2 + 7; the authored pair (7, 58) is the exception.
reasoning: Check 58 - 7^2 = 9, which disagrees with the same offset.
Compute 88 - 9^2 = 7. Three offsets equal 7; precisely one equals 9.
authored_transfer.independent_check: Substitute each input in y = x^2 + 7. For x = 7 it predicts 56, not the authored output 58; the remaining three outputs agree.

exit_task.prompt: AUTHORED INDEPENDENT EXIT (not Q003). A learner sees the ordered pairs (2, 9), (3, 14), (5, 30), (6, 43). Compute y - x^2 for each pair without changing the formula. Which pair fails the common rule? Explain why checking only the first pair would be insufficient.

answer.summary: The common residual is +5; (6, 43) is the exception because 43 - 6^2 = 7 rather than 5.
reasoning: 43 - 6^2 = 7, so the same y = x^2 + 5 rule fails only there.
One successful pair cannot establish a pattern; each given pair must be checked.

relations.meaning: For the proposed relation y = x^2 + k, the residual k is calculated the same way for every ordered pair (x, y); one exception is identified without changing the rule per pair.

symbols.meaning: square-offset residual for a matching group

conditions: Each ordered pair keeps x as its first coordinate and y as its second.
The hypothesized family is y = x^2 + k, and the same k must be used for all pairs claimed to match.
Matching a finite collection supports this candidate relation for those displayed observations, not a universal function theorem.

derivation.action: Subtract x squared from both sides of y = x squared + k.
derivation.why_valid: Subtracting the same integer from equal quantities preserves equality.

limits: Other models could also fit a finite collection of points; the item asks for the intended common relation and one differing case.
Changing the formula or input-output orientation independently for each option does not test one common rule.
checks: Compute y - x squared for every candidate pair and list each residual.
Apply the same proposed k to each pair claimed to match, and explain exactly which pair differs.

representations.purpose: Stage an unchanged residual calculation on newly authored pairs: fix the input-output direction, compare two consistent offsets, and show why one later offset differs.
required_elements: One fixed residual expression for every pair
Numerical agreement and an explicitly labelled exceptional residual
read_order: Read the first coordinate as input x and second as output y.
Compute y - x squared on the same basis for two pairs.
Compare the other two residuals and isolate the mismatch.
instance_constraints: Only separately authored transfer pairs appear in this visual; never draw Q003 source options.
At each stage the original authored pair values and the same residual formula are preserved.
accessibility: Each computed comparison is written in text and not only conveyed through colour.
The two-stage learner view has a descriptive SVG title, description, and readable labels.
misleading_alternatives: Changing k between pairs to force agreement.
Highlighting one answer without computing comparable residuals.

reveal_stages.purpose: Show the remaining authored calculations; one residual differs.
